subject: Private K8s delivery: peering, L2 segmentation and persistent dataset lifecycle
messages:
From: Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@cedarpoint-analytics.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-23T13:15:00-04:00
Subject: Private K8s delivery: peering & dataset lifecycle

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the quick intro earlier. We are kicking off the internal intake for CedarPoint's private deployment and want to capture network and storage constraints up front so the SOW and runbook match our ops expectations. High level asks: 

- Multi-site cluster (primary + DR) with private peering to our GCP VPC (no internet egress from control plane)
- L2 segmentation between tenant workloads and infra services (prometheus, logging)
- Two node profiles: compute-GPU for inference, and storage-medium for IO-heavy preprocessing
- Persistent datasets (2–5TB per tenant), want lifecycle policy: hot SSD for 30d, warm HDD for 180d, archive to object store after 1y
- Audit requirements: KMS integration and per-request audit logs for model inputs for 90 days

I attached a short ops checklist and a CSV of our site inventory. Can we run a 45-minute design workshop next week to lock node sizing, PV class mapping, and routing plan? 

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Neil
Head of Platform Ops | CedarPoint Analytics
[Attachment: cedarpoint-network-checklist.pdf (PDF, 90KB)]
[Attachment: cedarpoint-site-inventory.csv (CSV, 14KB)]

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@cedarpoint-analytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-23T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private K8s delivery: peering & dataset lifecycle

Hi Liam — thanks for the checklist and inventory. We're aligned on the big picture; a 45-minute workshop next Tue/Wed works. Preliminary notes before the workshop so we come prepared: 

- Peering model: prefer private VPN or cloud interconnect to avoid public IPs on control plane. We'll propose two routing options (VPC peering with restricted egress vs. NATed egress limited to logging endpoints).
- L2 segmentation: isolation by namespace + Cilium NetworkPolicies and a dedicated infra node pool (taints + tolerations) for telemetry. If they require hardware VLANs we can map them to node labels at provisioning.
- Node profiles: propose three node pools — gpu-infer (A100/80GB), cpu-workload (m5-like), storage-slice (NVMe ephemeral for caching + backing PVCs on blockstore). We'll bring sizing templates.
- PV lifecycle: we can implement a TTL-based move job that moves snapshots to an S3-compatible object store after the warm window. We'll need customer retention policy and egress constraints to size bandwidth for archival.
- KMS/audit: we can integrate with customer KMS (Cloud KMS or HSM) and stream audit logs to a controlled S3 bucket; clarify if audit logs must be encrypted with customer key.

I'll run the workshop invite once we settle a time. Can Karthik and Monica prepare node sizing guidance and recommended storage-class names so we can reference them in the SOW?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Technical Account Manager | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Private Deployments Team

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@cedarpoint-analytics.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-24T09:08:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Private K8s delivery: peering & dataset lifecycle

Vanessa / Liam — attaching a short matrix we'll use in the workshop. Quick technical clarifications ahead of the call: 

- Node pool breakdown (proposed):
  * gpu-infer: 3x A100-80GB per AZ (spot allowed for non-critical training jobs, but production inference must be on reserved nodes)
  * cpu-standard: 6x 16vCPU / 64GB (for orchestration, batching, and non-GPU workers)
  * storage-slice: 8x 24TB NVMe-backed nodes with local LVM for cache and csi-attached blockstore for PVCs

- Storage classes: 
  * redwood-fast-ssd (RWO, encrypted, replication=3)
  * redwood-warm-hdd (RWO, async-replicated to object store)
  * redwood-archive (object-backend, snapshot lifecycle)

- Eviction and QoS: we'll recommend QoS Class BestEffort only for ephemeral preproc; any model-serving pod should be Guaranteed/Burstable with local PVs pinned through node affinity to avoid noisy neighbor I/O.

- Network peering / egress: if customer cannot allow any egress, we'll run the control plane in their VPC; otherwise we'll suggest split control plane (control plane in Redwood Private with private peering for data plane) as a fallback.

I'll bring the Sizing worksheet to the workshop (see attachment).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Liam — confirmed for Wed 2026-08-26 10:00 PDT (45m). Agenda below and pre-work requests so the session is productive: 

Agenda (45m):
1) 10m — Goals & SLOs: throughput/latency targets for inference, retention windows for datasets
2) 10m — Network model: private peering options, IP management, and egress constraints
3) 10m — Node pools & storage classes: sizing, taints, and PVC throughput expectations
4) 10m — Security & audit: KMS, envelope keys, and log retention
5) 5m — Action items & next steps (SOW draft owner, PoC acceptance criteria)

Pre-work (please upload to the shared Drive link if possible):
- Confirmation of required retention windows (hot/warm/archive) and any regulatory holds
- Representative dataset IO profile (iops, throughput per 1TB)
- Any disallowed outbound endpoints for egress (URLs/IPs)

Notes: we'll propose the three storage classes Karthik listed. If CedarPoint wants hardware VLANs, we'll map node labels in provisioning — otherwise we prefer CNI-enforced namespace segmentation to keep operations simpler.

See you Wed — I'll send calendar invite + Google Meet link and attach the workshop packet.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
